skill.name: seal
skill.description: Guides file and credential transfers through SEAL tools, using inboxes, recipient addresses, restricted local files, and secret-aware program execution.
skill.summary: Use SEAL CLI or MCP workflows to exchange files and secrets without pasting their contents into chat.
skill.author: seal-hq

security_audit.summary: Most flags identify Markdown backticks or authorized secret-handling examples, not unsafe execution or credential theft. Confirmed risks include direct remote installer execution, an unpinned executable package, and instructions to execute commands supplied by update responses. No evidence found of intentional credential exfiltration or instructions to manipulate this audit.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:26 and SKILL.md:102 recommend piping a mutable remote installer directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace both examples with reviewed, versioned release downloads, verified signatures or trusted checksums, and explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:25 starts an unpinned package through npx with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed sealnet-mcp version, document provenance checks, and require approval before installing or executing a new dependency.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:106 tells the agent to run a command from an update response without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Use a fixed, reviewed update procedure instead of response-provided commands, and require user approval for changes to installed software.

content.user_title: Exchange Files and Secrets with SEAL
content.value_statement: Large files and credentials are difficult to exchange through chat without exposing their contents. This skill guides SEAL transfers through inboxes, restricted files, and recipient-addressed links.
actual_capabilities: Documents CLI and MCP workflows for sending files, folders, dumps, and builds.
Guides user inbox pairing and recipient-addressed transfers between agents.
Explains requesting secrets into restricted files instead of chat messages.
Describes passing requested secrets to programs with output redaction.
Documents metadata inspection, expiry, revocation, and transfer error recovery.
Lists Python and JavaScript SDK entry points for SEAL integrations.
limitations: The skill contains instructions only; it requires a separate SEAL CLI, MCP server, or SDK and network access.
Encryption, redaction, and service behavior are described but cannot be verified from the supplied instruction file.
Transfers have size, expiry, and access limits; larger files may require user payment.
Installation guidance includes unverified remote script execution and an unpinned package; these require remediation before unattended use.

use_cases.title: Deliver build artifacts
use_cases.description: Use an approved SEAL installation to send a generated archive to the user's paired inbox and report its receipt.

use_cases.title: Provide runtime credentials
use_cases.description: Request a needed credential through SEAL and pass its restricted file path to the intended program without printing its value.

use_cases.title: Coordinate agent file handoffs
use_cases.description: Forward a file to a verified agent address, inspect delivery metadata, and revoke access when the transfer is no longer needed.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a received transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the approved SEAL tool, inspect metadata for [link]. Report its name, size, and expiry without opening the contents.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a transfer before receiving it.

prompt_templates.title: Send an archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Send [archive path] to my paired SEAL inbox using existing approved tools. Report the receipt, and ask before any payment or installation.

prompt_templates.title: Request a program credential
prompt_templates.prompt: Request [credential] through SEAL for [program]. Show verification words, use a restricted file or redacted execution, and never print the secret.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: provide a credential without putting its value in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a recipient-bound handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm [recipient address], then forward [file path] with existing approved SEAL tools. Inspect status and report expiry. Revoke only when I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a controlled transfer between agents.

output_examples.input: What would a metadata-only transfer check report?
output: Illustrative receipt: release-archive.zip, 240 MB, expires in one day.

output_examples.input: What should happen when a secret cannot be opened inline?
output: The transfer is marked as a secret, so inline access is blocked.
Use file mode and pass the restricted file path to the intended program.
Do not display the secret value.

output_examples.input: What happens if my transfer exceeds the free limit?
output: The transfer requires a paid tier.
Review the payment request before continuing.
The documented workflow resumes the same transfer after payment.

best_practices: Use reviewed, pinned installations and approve software changes; do not execute remote installers or update-response commands without verification.
Keep secrets in restricted files or redacted program execution, and verify request words and recipient addresses.
Inspect metadata first, explain expiry and payment requirements, and revoke transfers that are no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Pasting credentials into chat, printing secret files, or inserting secret values directly into command arguments.
Forwarding files to unverified addresses or treating ordinary share links as recipient-bound links.
Automatically paying, overriding confirmations without consent, or running commands supplied by untrusted update responses.

faq.question: Can I use this skill with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists all three tools. Actual transfers require an available SEAL CLI, MCP server, or SDK.

faq.question: Does the skill implement encryption itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents SEAL workflows and describes sender-side encryption. The supplied file does not include implementation code for verification.

faq.question: Can I transfer a credential without pasting it into chat?
faq.answer: The documented request flow returns a restricted file path. Pass that path to the intended program or use the redacted execution workflow.

faq.question: Are large transfers free?
faq.answer: The documentation describes a free size limit. Larger transfers require a user payment, and current prices must be checked with the service.

faq.question: Why might a received link fail?
faq.answer: It may be expired, revoked, already opened, password-protected, or addressed to another recipient. The skill provides recovery steps for these cases.

faq.question: Should the installation commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The guidance includes remote scripts and an unpinned executable package. Use reviewed releases, integrity checks, and explicit approval before installing.
